newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian court acquits Moslem of war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Croatian court acquits Moslem of war crimes.

text.p: A Croatian court on Friday acquitted a Bosnian Moslem charged with war crimes allegedly committed when he was an officer in former Yugoslavia's federal army (JNA), local media said.

The county court in the Adriatic port of Zadar found Mirsad Catic, now a Bosnian embassy official in Bonn, not guilty of ordering a 1991 bombardment of the town during which more than 30 civilians were reported killed and 120 buildings damaged.

Croatia also linked another 19 ex-JNA officers, including the current chief of staff of the Yugoslav army Momcilo Perisic, to the bombardment and on Thursday put them on trial in absentia for war crimes against Zadar civilians.

JNA forces backed a Serb minority rebellion in 1991, helping them seize almost a third of Croatia by January 1992, when a ceasefire was signed. Croatian troops recaptured two of the three Serb-held enclaves in 1995 offensives.
Catic, who was taken into Croatian custody in August, was the only one of the 20 defendants present in the court.
In explaining the verdict, Judge Dubravko Krpina said the court could not find sufficient evidence that Catic had commanding authority at the time, HINA said.
"Defence of the accused could not be refuted...and prosecution witnesses proved to be unreliable," Krpina said.
He said they based their testimony on hearsay, which was unacceptable.
Catic was subsequently released from the prison in Zadar.
Croatian state radio said the trial of Perisic and his fellow officers would resume in November.
